title: Extrapulmonary sampling
dek: Lymph node, pleura, CSF, bone, urine. Paucibacillary sites punish smear and sometimes NAAT. The anatomic site is part of the pretest.
story: Extrapulmonary TB is not one disease. Tuberculous lymphadenitis is common and relatively reachable (FNA + WRD + cytology). Pleural TB is often an immunological effusion with few bacilli — ADA and a pleural biopsy beat a smear. Osteoarticular TB is a surgical specimen problem. Genitourinary TB may give urine culture/NAAT. Miliary is a blood-and-lung problem that masquerades as “fever of unknown.”

CSF in meningitis is an emergency specimen: WRD on CSF, culture a large volume, do not wait for a third lumbar puncture to start therapy if the prior is high. See the meningitis treatment plate for steroids and ART timing.
Always look for a pulmonary companion — not because EPTB “doesn’t transmit,” but because a missed cavity is a missed source, a missed DST, and a missed infection-control decision.
deep: Xpert Ultra on CSF and FNA is WHO-supported; sensitivity is imperfect. Trace in CSF of a treatment-naive meningitic patient is not the same object as trace in a scarred lung.
Pleural fluid WRD sensitivity is middling; biopsy and ADA (in high-prevalence settings) still matter.
Blood Xpert is not a routine bacteremia test. Mycobacterial blood culture in advanced HIV is a different tool.
Do not use IGRA on CSF as a gold standard. Interferon in the CSF is research-y; diagnosis is NAAT/culture/clinical.

visual.caption: Sites with different bacillary loads and assay yields. CSF and node FNA are WRD-actionable. Pleura is a biopsy disease. Always hunt a lung.

example.title: Lymph-node Ultra trace, pulmonary Ultra negative
example.setup: Cervical node, HIV-negative adult, FNA Ultra trace, sputum Ultra not detected, CXR normal.

steps.title: Node is the disease site
steps.body: A negative sputum does not veto lymphadenitis. Trace on FNA in a treatment-naive node is a strong microbiologic clue.

steps.title: Culture the leftover FNA
steps.body: DST still matters. Cytology for caseating granulomas supports.

steps.title: Look for the source case
steps.body: Adult node TB is often reactivation; still do contacts if pulmonary disease is found anywhere in the cluster.

example.takeaway: Match the specimen to the lesion; do not demand sputum physics of a node.

check.prompt: For suspected TB meningitis, the immediate diagnostic move is:
choices: Wait for a 6-week culture before any therapy
CSF WRD plus culture of an adequate volume, and do not delay treatment when clinical prior is high
IGRA on blood as a rule-in for meningitis
check.answer: CSF WRD plus culture of an adequate volume, and do not delay treatment when clinical prior is high

whyWrong.IGRA on blood as a rule-in for meningiti: Not a disease test for TBM.

check.prompt: Pleural fluid smear is rarely positive. The higher-yield next microbiologic step is usually:
choices: Repeating smear on the same fluid ten times only
Pleural biopsy for histopathology plus culture/WRD, with ADA as a contextual adjunct in high-prevalence settings
check.answer: Pleural biopsy for histopathology plus culture/WRD, with ADA as a contextual adjunct in high-prevalence settings
check.why: Paucibacillary effusion: tissue beats fluid smear.

check.prompt: On the constellation plate, why does “still image lung” have substantial weight?
choices: Because all EPTB is smear 3+ pulmonary by definition
Because a missed pulmonary companion changes transmission, DST sampling, and infection control
Because CXR diagnoses node TB with 100% PPV
check.answer: Because a missed pulmonary companion changes transmission, DST sampling, and infection control
check.why: Always look for the airway-connected lesion.
